citation: Shirley T. High Residence, 2021 Prairie Avenue. Halftone of a photograph of the house from the walk south-west of it, its street front and south flank under snow; unknown photographer, undated. Reproduced on chicagology.com, Prairie Avenue, 2021 S. Prairie.
author: unknown photographer
date: undated (the Chicagology file name suggests 1930; Shirley T. High lived there until at least 1940)
describes_date: undated, after 1886 (James L. High bought the house that year)
repository: chicagology.com (secondary reproduction; the original holder is not named). Prairie library image a20-chicagology-2021-high-photo, 'Shirley T. High Residence 2021 Prairie Avenue', recorded there as 'link only'; the project's reference copy is the image store's (kevinrhaas/chicago-images, prairie-1904/files/a20-chicagology-2021-high-photo.jpg), committed at data/sources/assets/high_2021_photo_t3633/ with its attribution, as the owner directed on 2026-10-11 for the image gate's pictures.
locator: The whole print: the street front with its gable and turret, the arched porch and stoop, the south flank, the gabled south wing to the picture's right edge, the roofs and stacks, and a picket fence in the snow at the right.
rights_note: A secondary web reproduction whose original source and rights are not stated (the Prairie library's own ruling: 'unknown - link only'). Only forms, counts, places and proportions are read from it; nothing is derived from the image as an asset (no texture, no traced mesh), and the copy committed for the image gate (T-3633) is the store's, unaltered, with its attribution in the folder's README.

note: The one picture of 2021 Prairie this project reads. A coarse halftone caption-titled 'Shirley T. High Residence': a dark brick house of two storeys over a high basement under a steep front gable lit by three attic lights, a round turret with a slate cone at the front's north corner over a round-arched porch reached by a stoop climbing along the front from the north, broad square-headed lights, a gabled wing standing out from the south flank, a tall stack on the south flank and two more on the roof, and a picket fence. The library reads the view as from the north-west with a north wing; the 1911 Sanborn sheet draws the round at the front's north-west corner and the projection on the south flank, so the camera stands south-west and the wing is the south one. It is undated and later than 1886, so it is evidence of its own date; the house stood in 1904 (the 1911 sheet draws the same plan), so its forms are carried to 1904 as inferred.
what_it_supplies: the front gable, the turret and its cone, the arched porch and the stoop, against the 1911 sheet's plan
the storeys: a high basement, two storeys and an attic in the gable, and the south wing's three storeys of lights
the lights of the front, the south flank and the south wing's west face
the roofs' slate and the stacks' places
what_it_does_not_supply: colour: the print is a monochrome halftone
the north flank, the rear and the rear ranges
